24번.q: 24. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?Progressive educators and librarians are developing curricula to teach what we might call attention literacy. This means helping students recognize, for example, how the architecture of a social media feed or a news site is deliberately designed to distract or provoke them. Classes in media literacy traditionally cover how to evaluate the credibility of sources — now they also include recognizing clickbait, understanding the role of algorithms in what content is served up, and observing one's own patterns of distraction. A student might be tasked with tracking how many times they switch tasks or check their phone in an hour of homework, to raise self-awareness about fragmentation. Another lesson might involve unpacking the design of popular apps: Why does an app use infinite scrolling instead of pages? Why do notifications appear with specific colors and sounds? By treating these as deliberate design choices (often rooted in psychology and profit motives), young people become more critical users rather than passive consumers.
opts: Raising Media Awareness: Noticing Intended Manipulations
Can Students Learn to Identify the Credibility of Information?
Application Developers' Focus on Users' Activeness
The Dark Side of Algorithms: A Threat to Privacy
Using Social Media to Communicate: Treasure or Poison?

Workers demand dignity, and their labor becomes expensive. Production processes burn through an island, and energy is no longer cheap. The climate changes, and crops can no longer grow as ④abundantly as they once did. Frontiers are so important in these processes because they offer places ⑤which the new cheap things can be seized — and the cheap work of humans and other natures can be forcefully taken.

30. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?Some people are more likely to cheat and steal after purchasing "eco-friendly" products, probably because they feel licensed to do so since they morally account the "eco-friendly" choice as a "good" deed. Moral licensing has also been ①observed in the context of cooperation for the good of the environment. When people are reminded of deeds they have done that they know were harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of "eco-guilt." People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and ②restore balance. In their search for such a balance, people are ③reluctant to believe in "quick-fixes," because they want to re-establish the moral balance and escape the guilt as quickly and easily as possible. In the same way that people may change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies between attitudes and behavior, people may also change their ④evaluation of past environmentally burdening behaviors and future environmentally friendly behaviors. For instance, people are ⑤more likely to sign a petition addressing environmental damage after viewing evidence of human-caused environmental damage.

34번.q: 34. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?When we focus on the obvious aspects of media, we miss the changes that 　　　　　　　　　　. Most of us notice the obvious aspects of a new medium or technology while missing the more subtle aspects. Take, for example, the microwave oven. It was introduced in the early 1980s and revolutionized food preparation. Traditionally, one person spent the better part of an afternoon fixing an evening meal for a family. Now, it was possible to prepare foods very quickly, and this shortening of preparation time was liberating for the cooks in the family, most of whom tended to be women. But the short-term, obvious implications of greater convenience made it easy to overlook the long-term implications of no longer having one person fix food for the family to eat together at an evening meal. As time went on, fewer and fewer families sat down together to eat dinner. Meals that took a long time to prepare became a luxury of the past, except perhaps for special occasions. The effects of the microwave oven on family life were not anticipated and would have been difficult to foresee.

38. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?So if an individual is looking forward to a concert, say, the feeling of crowding enhances their enjoyment of the performance.Environmental psychologists make a distinction between the physical measurement of density (how many people are in a particular space) and crowding (the psychological feeling of not having enough space). ( ① ) Usually, high density is needed for the phenomenon of crowding, which makes people experience sensory overload, a lack of control, and rising stress and anxiety. ( ② ) However, some psychologists see crowding as neutral rather than invariably negative, and believe that people's moods and behaviors intensify as density increases. ( ③ ) But if they are dreading an event, crowding will make the person's experience of it even worse. ( ④ ) Put into a community setting, crowding may accentuate the dominant behavior — an aggressive group may turn violent as density rises. ( ⑤ ) Conversely, creating positive social spaces such as parks and pedestrian areas in high-density urban environments may help to lift the general mood and defuse tension.

41~42번.q:
41. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?The concept of "choice architecture," popularized in behavioral economics, highlights how the design of the environment in which choices are made can significantly influence the decisions people make. Algorithms are, in essence, (a)sophisticated architects of our digital environments. By curating what we see, what we are recommended, and what options are presented to us, they subtly, and sometimes not so subtly, nudge us towards (b)particular paths. While nudges can be used for beneficial purposes, such as encouraging healthier habits, they also carry the potential for manipulation, particularly when the underlying objectives of the architects are not aligned with the well-being or autonomy of the individual.

The question then becomes: how can we cultivate and protect our human agency in an increasingly algorithmic world? It requires a (c)conscious effort to maintain critical engagement with the technologies we use. It means actively seeking out diverse perspectives, (d)following algorithmic recommendations, and making deliberate choices that go against the predicted grain. It involves cultivating a healthy skepticism towards the seemingly objective outputs of algorithms and remembering that these systems are designed by humans with specific goals, and that their data is a (e)reflection of past realities, not necessarily a prescription for future flourishing.
*nudge: 가볍게 자극하다
